# path


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module plans a path to a goal and runs it. It imports from
`abhyasa.learner`, `abhyasa.models`, `abhyasa.sources` and
`abhyasa.tutor`. It has five parts:

- **Plan a walk**: the planner, the walk from a paper, a text, a topic
  or a goal, the rabbit holes, and the readers of a step.
- **Run a walk step**: the tutor note of a step, its check, and the
  notebook spec that runs in Leela.
- **Change a walk**: the history of the changes, Undo, and the edits of
  the walk path.
- **Courses**: a course to your goal, its stages, where you are and what
  comes next.
- **Find a source for each step**: research on the web and in your
  folders, with the agent that gathers a passage for each idea.

The stored walk (`journey`, `put_journey`,
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#walk_state))
is in `abhyasa.learner`, and the checks of a web source are in
`abhyasa.sources`. Research loads the explainer video of `abhyasa.show`
when it needs it, because that module imports this one.

Import the modules that this module uses. The heavy ones load inside the
functions that need them, so the import stays light.

## Plan a walk

A walk and its path: an ordered list of steps, one concept each, that
the learner can see and change. The module is `abhyasa.path`.

A learner often wants to learn more than one concept. “I want to learn
how LLMs work” needs tokenizers, embeddings, attention, transformers and
more, in a given order. A walk keeps that goal and that order on the
learning shelf.

The planner (one model call) proposes the steps. It uses the concepts on
the shelf when they fit. It makes new concepts for the topics that the
shelf does not have. Then the learner can change the path: move, skip,
mark as known, add and split steps.

A walk keeps the outcome of each check on its step, and
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#walk_state)
counts them. A concept that the learner learns anywhere is known in each
walk that has it. An old walk with no `mode` (a path, from before
0.0.16) becomes a topic walk once, in the background at the start of the
app, with its progress
([`walk_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_path)).

### Change the steps

`journey_step` makes one change to one step: up, down, skip, known, todo
or remove. `journey_add` adds a step at the end, or before another step.
A step of a walk gets a short check.

### The planner

The planner gets the goal and the learner profile as text. It also gets
the concepts on the shelf that are near the goal or that the learner
started. It returns the steps in order.

*The prompt that plans a path to `goal`. `srcmap` is the

plan go in the prompt only when you give them. The audience and your
words are in `<source>` markers: they are data, not instructions.

``` python
p = plan_prompt('Teach agentic engineering', audience='people who do not write code', no_code=True, asks='Use only the notebook.')
assert all(x in p for x in ('Who the walk is for', 'people who do not write code', 'No code:', 'Use only the notebook.'))
assert not any(x in plan_prompt('Teach agentic engineering') for x in ('Who the walk is for', 'No code:', 'The learner asks'))
p
```

#### The source map

A goal can name its sources, such as `course22p2` and `fastbook`. The
Start box files them as chips.
[`chip_docs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#chip_docs)
gives the documents of each chip that is in the vault: a folder, a repo,
a GitHub repo or one vault document.
[`source_map`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#source_map)
gives the planner, for each chip, its root and up to 40 documents, each
as its short title and its first heading. So the plan can name the
document of each step.

[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#plan) saves the

uses that concept and keeps its state. Each other step becomes a new

### Walks

A walk from a source has `mode='walk'`. It is the reading path: one step
for each idea, in reading order. Each step has the passage to read
(`read`) and the check to do (`check`).

[`_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#_check)
picks the check of one concept. It uses the stats and the profile of the
learner, as
[`Tutor.ask_on`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#tutor.ask_on)
does. abhyasa runs no code: when the chosen way is code, the check kind
is `notebook`, and the step runs in Leela. On a tool walk (`tool=True`),
or for a step that needs a library, its reason says so. A step that the
plan marks `hands='notebook'` gets it too.

[`short_check`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#short_check)
gives a short-answer check in a text way. A walk uses it when a demo or
an order check has no card. The way comes from the text ways of the
concept, or from all text ways. A code way is not in the list, because
its check is a code task.

from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning

ckl = temp_learning()
ck = short_check(ckl, AttrDict(slug='x', name='X', ways=['demo', 'code']))

#### A walk has a most number of steps

A long source, such as a docs site, can have 60 ideas or more. A walk of
that length is too long to finish, and each step costs model calls for
its note and its check. So a walk has at most `val('walks.steps')` steps
(7 by default, and 7 at most; you can change it on the Settings page). A
walk from a paper, a book or a page gets a *walk map*
([`walk_map`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_map),
the prompt `walk.map`): the claim of the source, and 3 to 7 big ideas
that a novice must understand to explain it. Each big idea has its
understanding, an essential question and its common wrong ideas. The
steps are the big ideas. Each other idea is a detail of one big idea: it
stays on the step as reading and in Words to know, with no check of its
own. A number, a score, a year, an ablation or a remark of the author is
never a big idea. When the map fails,
[`main_steps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#main_steps)
asks the model to pick the main ideas, with the prompt `walk.pick`. A
walk from one of your notebooks gets no map: its ideas are its sections.
When the reply has fewer valid numbers, the first ideas that are not
picked fill the walk in source order. The steps keep the order of the
source, and a prerequisite that is picked comes before the idea that
needs it. The pick happens when the walk is made, before any step writes
a note or a check. The other ideas stay on the shelf as concepts. The
walk keeps their slugs in `more`, so the plan can say how many more
ideas the source has.

### map_prompt

``` python
def map_prompt(
    cs, most:int, audience:str=''
)->str:
```

*The prompt that asks for the claim and the `most` big ideas of the
concepts `cs`, numbered from 1 in the order of the source. A detail is
marked.* `audience` says who the walk is for; it goes in a `<source>`
marker, as data and not as instructions.

The map keeps the big ideas in source order. Each one saves its core and
its wrong ideas, and the step keeps its essential question and its
details. A score is a detail of the idea that it supports.

``` python
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
ml = temp_learning()
for n, st in [('Attention', 'Each word weighs every word.'), ('Multi-head attention', 'Several attention heads run side by side.'),
              ('BLEU results', 'The big model reached 28.4 BLEU.'), ('Positional encoding', 'Sines give each position a code.')]: ml.put(n, st, 'ml')
mst = [dict(slug=s) for s in ('attention', 'multi-head-attention', 'bleu-results', 'positional-encoding')]
mfk = Fake({'Return JSON: {"claim"': dict(claim='Attention alone can translate well.', ideas=[
    dict(n=4, understanding='You understand that position codes tell attention the order, because attention alone ignores order.', question='How does the model know word order?', wrong=['attention reads words in order']),
    dict(n=1, understanding='Each word builds its new vector from all words, because it weighs them by match.', question='Why can attention look at all words at once?', details=[3, 1, 2])])})
ss, more, mp = walk_map(ml, mfk, mst)
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in ss], ['attention', 'positional-encoding'])
test_eq((ss[0]['details'], ss[0]['question'], more), (['bleu-results', 'multi-head-attention'], 'Why can attention look at all words at once?', ['multi-head-attention', 'bleu-results']))
test_eq(ml.concept('positional-encoding').core, 'position codes tell attention the order, because attention alone ignores order.')
test_eq(ml.concept('positional-encoding').wrong, [dict(think='attention reads words in order', fact='')])
test_eq(mp['claim'], 'Attention alone can translate well.')
```

A reply with no valid idea falls back to
[`main_steps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#main_steps),
and there is no map. Two steps get no map and no call.

``` python
ss, more, mp = walk_map(ml, Fake(), mst, most=3)
test_eq((len(ss), mp), (3, None))
n = Fake(); test_eq(walk_map(ml, n, mst[:2]), (mst[:2], [], None)); test_eq(n.calls, [])
```

A demo, an order check or a code task takes longer than a short answer.
So at most a share of the steps of a walk get one (the setting
`walks.hands`, a third by default, rounded down, and at least 1 in a
walk of 3 steps or more).
[`cap_hands`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#cap_hands)
counts the hands-on checks in walk order, after
[`main_steps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#main_steps).
When the walk has its share, each later step gets a check in its text
ways. The count does not depend on chance, so a test can check it. A
step that the plan marks `hands='notebook'` builds part of the goal, so
[`cap_hands`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#cap_hands)
leaves it as it is.
[`hands_count`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#hands_count)
counts it apart. The share only warns: the walk editor shows the counts,
and nothing stops a walk with more.

#### A walk from one of your notebooks

A notebook that you wrote is already a lesson, so the walk uses it as it
is. [`nb_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#nb_file)
finds the notebook file of a vault document.
[`nb_sections`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#nb_sections)
splits the notebook at the headings of its section level (the title at
the top is not a section).
[`notebook_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#notebook_walk)
makes one idea for each section, named by its heading. The passage of
the idea is the words and the code of the section, word for word
([`nb_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#nb_text)),
with its source line, so the trust rules of the walk stay: real,
verbatim and linked. The statement of the idea is the first sentence of
the section. The tutor adds only the check of each idea: a demo where
the code of the section draws a picture, else a check in the ways of the
idea. The walk keeps the path of the notebook in `notebook`. With three
sections or more, one model call, the walk map
([`walk_map`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_map)),
keeps the sections that teach a big idea, with the key question of each
and the main idea of the notebook. A setup section, as the imports,
leaves the plan but stays in the notebook. When the map gives nothing,
each section stays.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L460"

the document is a notebook that is on this Mac; else None.*

A notebook with a title, two sections and a subsection. The subsection
is in its section, and the cells before the first section are not one.

``` python
from fastcore.nbio import new_nb, mk_cell, write_nb
```

``` python
nbd = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'nbs'; nbd.mkdir()
NB_CELLS = [mk_cell('# DDPM\n\n> Denoising diffusion, from scratch', 'markdown'), mk_cell('import torch'),
            mk_cell('## Introduction', 'markdown'), mk_cell('The 2020 paper made some crucial assumptions that simplify the training of the model. Later models build on it.', 'markdown'),
            mk_cell('## Data loading', 'markdown'), mk_cell('We load Fashion MNIST, and we do not use its labels for this task.', 'markdown'), mk_cell('dls = get_dls()'),
            mk_cell('### Noise schedule', 'markdown'), mk_cell('The noise grows at each step of the forward process.', 'markdown'), mk_cell('show_images(noised)')]
nbp = nbd/'15_DDPM.ipynb'; write_nb(new_nb(NB_CELLS), nbp)
secs = nb_sections(read_nb(nbp).cells)
test_eq([(s.head, s.first, s.last) for s in secs], [('Introduction', 2, 3), ('Data loading', 4, 9)])
t = nb_text(read_nb(nbp).cells[4:10])
assert t.startswith('## Data loading') and '```python\ndls = get_dls()\n```' in t and '### Noise schedule' in t
```

The notebook goes on a notebook shelf, as Start files it. The walk has
one idea for each section, in the words and the code of the notebook,
and no model call. The section whose code draws gets a demo check.

``` python
from abhyasa.sources import index_notebooks
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
nl, nf = temp_learning(), Fake({})
index_notebooks(nl.vault, [nbd])
nd = first(nl.doc_shelf('notebooks').t.docs())
nw = journey_from_source(nl, nf, nd['id'], 'notebooks')
test_eq(nf.calls, [])   # no model call: the notebook is used as it is
test_eq([nl.concept(s['slug']).name for s in nw.steps], ['Introduction', 'Data loading'])
test_eq(Path(nw.notebook['path']).resolve(), nbp.resolve())
r0, r1 = nw.steps[0]['read'], nw.steps[1]['read']
assert r0['text'].startswith('## Introduction') and r0['section'] == 'Introduction' and r0['doc_id'] == nd['id'] and r0['cells'] == [2, 3]
assert 'dls = get_dls()' in r1['text']
test_eq((nw.steps[1]['check']['kind'], nw.steps[1]['check']['why']), ('demo', NB_WHY_DEMO))   # its code draws a picture
test_eq(nl.concept(nw.steps[0]['slug']).statement, 'The 2020 paper made some crucial assumptions that simplify the training of the model.')
```

With three sections or more, the walk map keeps the sections that teach
a big idea. The imports leave the plan, each idea gets its key question,
and the walk keeps the main idea.

``` python
nbp4 = nbd/'16_DDPM_v2.ipynb'
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# DDPM again', 'markdown'), mk_cell('## Imports', 'markdown'), mk_cell("We'll start with some imports.", 'markdown'), mk_cell('import torch'),
                 mk_cell('## Noise', 'markdown'), mk_cell('The forward process adds a little noise at each step, so the last step is pure noise.', 'markdown'),
                 mk_cell('## Model', 'markdown'), mk_cell('A U-Net learns to predict the noise that was added to an image.', 'markdown'),
                 mk_cell('## Sampling', 'markdown'), mk_cell('We start from noise and take away the predicted noise, step by step.', 'markdown')]), nbp4)
index_notebooks(nl.vault, [nbd])
d4 = first(r for r in nl.doc_shelf('notebooks').t.docs() if '16_DDPM_v2' in r['meta'])
ideas = [dict(n=n, understanding=f'Idea {n} does this because of that.', question=q, wrong=[], details=[]) for n, q in ((2, 'Why does the noise grow?'), (3, 'What does the model predict?'), (4, 'How does a picture come out of noise?'))]
mf = Fake({'Ideas, in the order of the source': dict(claim='A model that learns to remove noise can make new pictures from noise.', ideas=ideas)})
mw = journey_from_source(nl, mf, d4['id'], 'notebooks')
test_eq(len(mf.calls), 1)
test_eq([nl.concept(s['slug']).name for s in mw.steps], ['Noise', 'Model', 'Sampling'])   # Imports teaches no idea of the notebook
test_eq([s['question'] for s in mw.steps], [x['question'] for x in ideas])
test_eq((mw.map['claim'], [nl.concept(s).name for s in mw.more]), ('A model that learns to remove noise can make new pictures from noise.', ['Imports']))
test_eq([s['read']['cells'] for s in mw.steps], [[4, 5], [6, 7], [8, 9]])   # each idea keeps its cells, so Leela opens at its section
```

The learner learns the notebook in Leela.
[`learning_copy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#learning_copy)
writes a learning copy for Leela in the folder of the walk
([`copy_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#copy_path),
in the vault assets): the notebook as it is, with the demo of each idea
as a \`\`\`rupaka block in a markdown cell after its section. Leela
draws the block. The learner’s own notebook is only read. A copy at the
path of the notebook itself is refused.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L496"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### learning_copy

``` python
def learning_copy(
    j, dest, demos:NoneType=None
)->pathlib.Path:
```

*Write the learning copy of the notebook of walk `j` to `dest`: the
notebook as it is, with the demo of each idea (`demos` maps a slug* to a
rupaka spec) as a markdown cell with a
\`\``rupaka block after the last cell of its section. Leela draws the block. The learner's own notebook is only read, never written. Return`dest\`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L492"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### copy_path

``` python
def copy_path(
    assets, j
)->pathlib.Path:
```

*The path of the learning copy of the notebook of walk `j`:
`<assets>/walks/<walk id>/<name of the notebook>`, in the folder of the
walk.*

The copy has one more cell, the demo, after the last cell of its
section. The notebook file has the same bytes as before.

``` python
spec = dict(id='noise-demo', title='Noise', state={}, blocks=[])
dest = copy_path(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'assets', nw)
test_eq((dest.parent.name, dest.parent.parent.name, dest.name), (nw.id, 'walks', '15_DDPM.ipynb'))
was = nbp.read_bytes()
learning_copy(nw, dest, {nw.steps[1]['slug']: spec})
cp = read_nb(dest)
test_eq(len(cp.cells), len(NB_CELLS) + 1)
assert cp.cells[10].source.startswith('**A demo: Data loading.**') and '```rupaka' in cp.cells[10].source and '"noise-demo"' in cp.cells[10].source
test_eq(nbp.read_bytes(), was)   # your own notebook does not change
test_fail(lambda: learning_copy(nw, nbp, {}), contains='your own notebook')
```

[`journey_from_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#journey_from_sources)
makes one walk across many pages, for example the pages of a docs site
that
[`file_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_link)
filed. The tutor reads each page in turn. The steps come in page order,
and in each page in the order of the page. An idea that two pages name
gets one step, in the first page where its passage is. When no page has
its passage, the step is in the first page that names it.
`progress(k, n)` hears of page `k` of `n` before the tutor reads it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L519"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### journey_from_sources

``` python
def journey_from_sources(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, docs:list, title:str='', subject:str='', progress:NoneType=None,
    tool:bool=False, audience:str='', no_code:bool=False, **extra
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Make one walk across the vault documents `docs`, each with `shelf`,
`doc_id`, `title` and `url`, in their order. `extra` goes on the walk.*
`audience` (who the walk is for) goes to the walk map; with `no_code`,
no check is code. The walk keeps both.

[`walk_from_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_from_topic)
plans a path to the goal. With the chips of the Start box, the planner
sees the source map and the data list, and each step reads the paragraph
of its `doc` that names the most main words of the idea, and at least
half of them. A step with no `doc` reads the first passage in your
sources that names the idea or an alias. A passage from a source that
the goal named may instead name every main word of the idea. A weak
match is no source: the step has no `read`, the page shows the tutor’s
words, and research can look on the web.

#### Your data

A course or a walk can keep folders of your own data in `data`, as a
list of `{path, note}`, or `{path, note, name}` when you gave the folder
the data name of a step. abhyasa does not file these folders and does
not learn from them. The exercises run on them in Leela.
[`data_row`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#data_row)
checks one folder, and
[`keep_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#keep_data)
adds it to a list.
[`data_entries`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#data_entries)
makes the data entries of a notebook spec: the name of the row, else an
upper-case name from the folder name, the path, and `what`, with the
note and a short listing of the folder. A row with no `name` (an older
row) still works: it gets a name from its folder.

[`with_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#with_data)
puts the entries of a step on these folders. The folders of the walk (a
course gives its folders to each of its walks) are the one set of data
names. An entry never keeps a path that the model wrote: an entry with
the name or the path of a folder gets the name and path of that folder,
and any other entry keeps its name and `what` with no path and
`need: true`. That is a folder that the learner must add under Your
data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L589"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

)->list:
```

*The data entries `entries` on your data folders
[`rows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#rows) only,
then an entry for each folder that they do not name, at most `DATA_MOST`
in all.* An entry with the name or the path of a folder gets that
folder. Any other entry has no path and `need`: the learner adds its
folder.

```

### data_row

``` python
def data_row(
    path, note:str='', name:str=''
)->dict:
```

*The data folder `path` as a row `{path, note}` (and `name`, when
given), with `~` for the home folder. A `ValueError` says in one line
why abhyasa cannot use it.*

A folder in your home folder is a data row, with `~` and its note. A
path outside the home folder, a path that is not a folder, and a ninth
folder are refused, each with one plain line. Here the home folder is a
temporary folder.

``` python
home, old = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(), os.environ['HOME']
os.environ['HOME'] = str(home)
try:
    (eps := home/'ramayana-episodes').mkdir(); (eps/'episodes.json').write_text('{}'); (eps/'characters.json').write_text('[]'); (eps/'.hidden').write_text('')
    rows = keep_data([], str(eps), 'The 418 episodes:\nmy scenarios run on them.')
    test_eq(rows, [dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='The 418 episodes: my scenarios run on them.')])
    test_eq(keep_data(rows, '~/ramayana-episodes', 'New note.'), [dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='New note.')])   # one row for each path
    for bad, said in (('/etc', 'not in your home folder'), (str(eps/'episodes.json'), 'no folder'), ('~/nothing', 'no folder')):
        with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, said): keep_data(rows, bad)
    with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, 'at most 8'): keep_data([dict(path=f'~/d{k}', note='') for k in range(8)], str(eps))
    es = data_entries(rows)
finally: os.environ['HOME'] = old
test_eq(es, [dict(name='RAMAYANA_EPISODES', path='~/ramayana-episodes', what='The 418 episodes: my scenarios run on them. It holds: characters.json, episodes.json.', need=False)])
```

A name that a step uses already gets a number.
[`with_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#with_data)
keeps the entries of the step first, and adds only the folders that they
do not name. An entry on a folder gets the name of the folder. Each
entry passes the check of a notebook spec.

``` python
from abhyasa.contract import validate_nb_spec, _GOOD
```

``` python
test_eq([e['name'] for e in data_entries([dict(path='~/x/2024 data', note=''), dict(path='~/y/2024-data', note='')], taken=['D_2024_DATA'])], ['D_2024_DATA_2', 'D_2024_DATA_3'])
step = [dict(name='IMAGES', path='~/Pictures/comic', what='your images', need=True)]
test_eq([e['name'] for e in with_data(step, [dict(path='~/Pictures/comic', note=''), dict(path='~/ramayana-episodes', note='')])], ['COMIC', 'RAMAYANA_EPISODES'])
test_eq(validate_nb_spec({**_GOOD, 'data': es})['data'], es)
```

A row with a `name` keeps that name, also when a folder without a name
would take it. A note that ends with a stop gets no second stop:

``` python
rows = [dict(path='~/x/episodes', note=''), dict(path='~/y/comics', note='The text of the comic episodes.', name='EPISODES')]
test_eq([(e['name'], e['what']) for e in data_entries(rows)], [('EPISODES_2', 'Your data folder.'), ('EPISODES', 'The text of the comic episodes.')])
test_eq((with_stop('Text of the episodes'), with_stop('Text of the episodes.'), with_stop('Why?'), with_stop('')), ('Text of the episodes.', 'Text of the episodes.', 'Why?', ''))
```

With no folders, a path that the model wrote goes, and the entry keeps
its name and `what`. The learner adds that folder.

``` python
invented = [dict(name='EPISODES', path='~/comics/episodes.txt', what='the text of your comic episodes', need=False), dict(name='IMAGES', path='~/comic_images', what='your images', need=False)]
test_eq(with_data(invented, None), [dict(name='EPISODES', path='', what='the text of your comic episodes', need=True), dict(name='IMAGES', path='', what='your images', need=True)])
test_eq(validate_nb_spec({**_GOOD, 'data': with_data(invented, [])})['data'][0]['path'], '')
```

With a folder of that name, the entry gets its path. A second entry on
the same folder goes.

``` python
test_eq([(e['name'], e['path'], e['need']) for e in with_data([*invented, {**invented[0], 'what': ''}], [dict(path='~/x/episodes', note='')])],
        [('EPISODES', '~/x/episodes', False), ('IMAGES', '', True)])
```

Across a walk, one folder has one name.
[`walk_names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_names)
gives the data names that the other steps of the walk use.
[`same_names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#same_names)
gives an entry the name that the walk uses for the same `what`, also in
the text of the spec.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L614"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### same_names

``` python
def same_names(
    spec, named
)->dict:
```

*Notebook spec `spec` with each data entry whose `what` is the `what` of
an entry in `named` (the walk names it) under the name of that entry.*
The name changes in the task, the stub and the run too, so they name the
same data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L604"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### walk_names

``` python
def walk_names(
    j, i:int | None=None
)->list:
```

*The data entries `{name, what}` that the notebook specs of the steps of
walk `j` (not step `i`) name: the first entry for each name and for each
`what`.*

Steps 1 and 2 name the same images, so the walk keeps only the first
name, IMAGES:

``` python
eps = dict(name='EPISODES', what='Text file of the comic episodes.')
j2 = AttrDict(steps=[dict(nb=dict(data=[eps, dict(name='IMAGES', what='The comic images.')])), dict(nb=dict(data=[dict(name='COMIC_IMAGES', what='the comic images')])), dict()])
test_eq(walk_names(j2, 1), [eps, dict(name='IMAGES', what='The comic images.')])
test_eq([d['name'] for d in walk_names(j2)], ['EPISODES', 'IMAGES'])   # the second name for the same images is not a new name
```

A new spec that calls the images COMIC_IMAGES gets IMAGES. A longer name
that starts the same way stays as it is:

``` python
mine = dict(task='Load COMIC_IMAGES.', stub='def f(): pass', data=[dict(name='COMIC_IMAGES', path='', what='The comic images', need=True)],
            run=dict(say='Write the run here: read COMIC_IMAGES and COMIC_IMAGES_2.', predict=''))
got = same_names(mine, walk_names(j2))
test_eq((got['task'], got['data'][0]['name'], got['run']['say']), ('Load IMAGES.', 'IMAGES', 'Write the run here: read IMAGES and COMIC_IMAGES_2.'))
assert same_names(mine, []) is mine
```

#### The data that a walk still needs

[`missing_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#missing_data)
gives the data entries `{name, what}` that the notebook steps of a walk
name and that have no folder under Your data. With `i`, it looks only at
step `i`. The page asks for each one with one short line:
[`data_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#data_line)
keeps the first sentence of `what`
([`short_what`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#short_what)),
with no second stop.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L646"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

```

*The data entries `{name, what}` that the notebook specs of walk `j` (or
of step `i` only) name, and that no folder under Your data (`j.data`)
has.*

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L642"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### data_line

``` python
def data_line(
    d
)->str:
```

*The line for data entry `d` that has no folder:
`EPISODES: the text of the comic episodes.` The page puts the action
(Set it) after it.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L632"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### short_what

``` python
def short_what(
    w, most:int=80
)->str:
```

*The first sentence of `w`, at most about `most` characters, with no
stop at its end and no “folder of” at its start, to go after a name and
a colon.* Each word keeps its case. Only a first word that is a common
word (`COMMON`, or a word before “of”) gets a small letter, so “Indian”
stays.

The line has the name, a short form of `what` and one stop, and no
action: the page adds Set it. A long `what` is cut at a word:

``` python
test_eq(data_line(dict(name='EPISODES', what='Text of the comic episodes. Short caption lines are taken from it and used as prompts.')),
        'EPISODES: the text of the comic episodes.')
test_eq(data_line(dict(name='IMAGES', what='Folder of your own Indian comic panel images. Name the folder you want to use.')),
        'IMAGES: your own Indian comic panel images.')
test_eq(data_line(dict(name='RAMAYANA', what='')), 'The folder of RAMAYANA.')
long = short_what('A very long description of the images ' * 4)
assert len(long) <= 81 and long.startswith('a very') and long.endswith('…') and '..' not in long
```

A word with a capital keeps it. Only a common first word, as “The” or
“A”, gets a small letter:

``` python
test_eq(short_what('Indian comic page or panel images (jpg or png) that you choose and name.'), 'Indian comic page or panel images (jpg or png) that you choose and name')
test_eq(short_what('Ramayana episodes as JSON.'), 'Ramayana episodes as JSON')
test_eq([short_what(x) for x in ('The comic images.', 'A list of names.', 'PNG panels.')], ['the comic images', 'a list of names', 'PNG panels'])
```

Step 0 names EPISODES and IMAGES. With a folder named EPISODES under
Your data, only IMAGES is missing. Step 2 has no notebook:

``` python
j3 = AttrDict(steps=[dict(nb=dict(data=[eps, dict(name='IMAGES', what='The comic images.')])), dict(nb=dict(data=[dict(name='IMAGES', what='the comic images')])), dict()], data=[])
test_eq([d['name'] for d in missing_data(j3)], ['EPISODES', 'IMAGES'])
test_eq([d['name'] for d in missing_data({**j3, 'data': [dict(path='~/comics', note='', name='EPISODES')]})], ['IMAGES'])
test_eq(missing_data(j3, 2), [])
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L744"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### walk_from_topic

``` python
def walk_from_topic(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, goal:str, who:str='', sources:NoneType=None, tool:bool=False, chips:tuple=(),
    data:tuple=(), audience:str='', no_code:bool=False, asks:str='', owner:str='', near:bool=True
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Plan a path to `goal` and make it a walk of at most `walks.steps`
steps, with a passage and a check on each step. With `chips` (the* chip
ids of the Start box), the planner sees the
[`source_map`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#source_map).
With `data` (your data folders, `{path, note}`), the planner sees their
data entries, and the walk keeps them. `audience` (who the walk is for)
and `no_code` go to the planner and stay on the walk; `asks` (what you
ask for this plan) goes only to the planner, and so does `owner`, as an
instruction of the owner
([`owner_says`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#owner_says)).

[`minutes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#minutes)
guesses the time for one step: reading at 200 words a minute, plus the
time of its check.

```

### Rabbit holes

A step can need an idea that you have not learned. For example, the
scaling by √dk in a paper on attention needs gradients. These functions
find what is missing, make a short side walk on it, and link the side
walk back to the step.

[`needs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#needs) lists
the prereqs of a concept, then its gaps. A need is met at depth `READY`
(3) or more, as in `model.ready`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L771"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### needs

``` python
def needs(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, slug:str, by:dict=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*The prereqs, then the gaps, of concept `slug` that are on the shelf.
`ok` is true at depth `READY` or more.*

[`walk_needs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_needs)
gives each need of a step a state by the same count as the walk
([`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#walk_state)).
A need that is a step of this walk that you closed solid is `done`, with
`at`, its index. A need that you closed shaky is `shaky`. Else a need in
`met` (a side walk today) is `today`, also when its side check made it
ready, a need at depth `READY` is
[`learned`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#learned),
and the rest is `missing`. So the line never says “not learned yet” for
an idea that the walk just did.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L783"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### walk_needs

``` python
def walk_needs(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, j, i:int, by:dict=None, met:tuple=()
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*The needs of step `i` of walk `j`
([`needs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#needs)), each
with `state`: done, shaky, learned, today or missing, and `at`, the
index of the step that did it.*

[`known_how`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#known_how)
says how you know one idea at a step, by the same rule, for a gap that
your answer showed. A side walk from this step that ended solid or
fragile is `side`. Then the steps of this walk count (`done`, `shaky`),
then a side walk that ended shaky, then the depth on the shelf
([`learned`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#learned)).
Else the idea is `missing`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L795"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### known_how

``` python
def known_how(
    j, i:int, slug:str, by:dict
)->tuple:
```

*How you know concept `slug` at step `i` of walk `j`: `(state, index)`,
with state side, done, shaky, learned or missing, and the index of the
step that did it.*

[`pick_way_down`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#pick_way_down)
picks how to learn a missing idea:

- `primer`: one step and one short check. You met the idea before (depth
  1 or 2), or it needs no other idea that you have not learned.
- `walk`: a side walk on the chain, at most `walks.chain` (4 by default)
  ideas. The chain is the unready prereqs, deepest first, then the idea.
- `course`: a big topic. The gap is more than `walks.chain` ideas on the
  shelf, or the tutor said that the idea builds on `COURSE_AT` (6) ideas
  or more when it added it (`size`). It opens as its own course, with a
  level check and stages.

The size of the gap picks the depth. The learner can always pick one of
the other two.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L822"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

```

*How to learn concept `slug` before you go on: a quick `primer`, a side
`walk`, or its own `course`, with why in one line.* The gap is the
unready prereqs on the shelf, or the size that the tutor gave, the
larger of the two.

```

[`detour`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#detour) makes
the side walk and starts it. It keeps `parent` (the walk and the step
that opened it) and `depth`. A side walk of a side walk has depth 2.
Past `walks.depth` (2 by default), only its own session can open, at
depth 0. With no chain on the shelf, the side walk is a short path that
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#plan) makes,
with steps as
[`walk_from_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_from_topic)
makes them. The planned walk is not kept. It always ends on the idea.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L847"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Make and start a side walk on concept `slug`, as a child of `parent`
(`{walk, step}`, or a place in Leela).*

[`parent_step`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#parent_step)
gives the walk and the step that opened side walk `j`, when both are
still there. Else it gives `(None, None)`. The walk page, the side pane,
the history and the walk list use it, so they agree on “the parent step
is still there”. With `js`, a dictionary of walks by id, it reads no
walk from the shelf.

[`trail`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#trail) gives
the walks from the root walk down to a side walk, for the crumbs.
[`back_from`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#back_from)
keeps the result of a side walk on the step that opened it, in
`detours`. The result is the outcome of the last step, or `skipped`. One
side walk has one record. When you come back again with a new outcome,
the record changes, and `at` is the time of the new outcome. A later
skip does not change a record.

[`for_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#for_talk)
tells a walk that is for the room: a side walk that a talk opened (its
parent is `{talk, slide}`), or the walk that a talk was made from, from
a path, a walk with no source (its parent is `{journey, for: 'talk'}`).
Such a walk is not your own learning, so the pages that list your walks
and the steps you read skip it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L908"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### for_talk

``` python
def for_talk(
    j
)->bool:
```

*Whether walk `j` is for a talk: a side walk that a talk opened beside a
slide, or the walk that a talk was made from, from a path.*

A walk with a talk parent, or one made for a talk from a path, is for
the room. A walk with a walk parent, or with no parent, is your own.

``` python
assert for_talk(dict(parent={'talk': 't-1', 'slide': 's3'})) and not for_talk(dict(parent={'walk': 'w-1', 'step': 0}))
assert for_talk(dict(parent={'journey': 'j-1', 'for': 'talk'})) and not for_talk(dict(parent={'journey': 'j-1'}))
assert not for_talk({}) and not for_talk(None) and not for_talk(dict(parent=None))
```

A talk from your sources has a hidden walk under it, so the talk builder
and each rebuild read `src.walk` as before.
[`file_chip`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#file_chip)
files the source of one chip of the Start box, or finds the documents of
a chip that is in the vault.
[`walk_for_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_for_talk)
files the chips and makes the walk, with `parent={'for': 'talk'}`, so
[`for_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#for_talk)
hides it. With a goal, it is a goal walk, as Start makes it. With no
goal and one notebook as the only source, it is one step for each
section of the notebook, in order
([`notebook_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#notebook_walk)
with no walk map), so no idea is renamed or moved. Else it is one walk
across the documents. The walk keeps `audience` and `no_code`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L934"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*File the chips `chips`, and make and save the hidden walk of a talk
from them.
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said) gets each
stage. The walk of one notebook takes the title of the notebook
([`nb_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#nb_title)).*
`owner` (what the owner asks for, such as the roles of the sources) goes
to the planner
([`owner_says`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#owner_says)),
and the walk keeps it as its `change`, so the slide writer gets it too.

```

### file_chip

``` python
def file_chip(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, i:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*The documents of the chip id `i`: it files a `gh:`, `folder:`, `repo:`,
`file:` or `link:` source, and finds a `vault:` or `doc:` one.*

A notebook with three sections, under a home folder for the test, gives
a hidden walk with one step for each section, in order, and no model
call. The walk takes the first `#` heading of the notebook as its title,
not the name of its vault document. These tests need their own imports.

``` python
import os, tempfile
from fastcore.nbio import new_nb, mk_cell, write_nb
from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
twh, twold = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(), os.environ['HOME']
os.environ['HOME'] = str(twh)
try:
    twp = twh/'talks'/'agents.ipynb'; twp.parent.mkdir()
    write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# Agents', 'markdown'), mk_cell('## Tool calls', 'markdown'), mk_cell('The model names a tool, and the agent runs it.', 'markdown'),
                     mk_cell('## The agent loop', 'markdown'), mk_cell('print(2 + 3)'), mk_cell('## Memory between turns', 'markdown')]), twp)
    twl, twf = temp_learning(), Fake({})
    tww = walk_for_talk(twl, twf, [f'file:{twp}'], audience='Engineers who are new to agents', no_code=True)
finally: os.environ['HOME'] = twold
test_eq([twl.concept(s['slug']).name for s in tww.steps], ['Tool calls', 'The agent loop', 'Memory between turns'])
assert for_talk(tww) and twf.calls == [] and tww.chips == [f'file:{twp}'] and tww.title == 'Agents'
(tww.audience, tww.no_code, tww.notebook['path'] == str(twp))
```

A notebook with no `#` heading takes its file name in words, with no
number at its start.

``` python
ntp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'02_agentic_engineering.ipynb'
write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('## Tool calls', 'markdown')]), ntp)
test_eq(nb_title(ntp), 'Agentic engineering')
```

[`walk_from_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_from_talk)
makes a walk of your own from the hidden walk of a talk. You use it
after a talk on a topic, to learn the topic yourself. The new walk has
the steps of the hidden walk in the order of the slides, and no
`parent`, so it shows on Home. The talk gives the order, because this
module does not read talks. A step that is not in the order is left out.
The new walk keeps the notebook, the sources and who it is for, and none
of the progress of the hidden walk.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L957"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### walk_from_talk

``` python
def walk_from_talk(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str, order
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Make and save a walk of your own from the hidden walk `jid` of a talk:
its steps in the order of the concept slugs `order` (the slides), with
no `parent` and no progress.*

A hidden walk with three steps, and a talk with two of them in another
order, gives a walk with those two steps in the talk order. It has no
`parent`, so it is not for a talk, and no step keeps its progress.

``` python
wl = temp_learning()
hw = wl.put_journey(dict(id='agents-h1', title='Agents', goal='Read Agents', mode='walk', parent={'for': 'talk'}, chips=['file:/u/k/a.ipynb'], notebook=dict(path='/u/k/a.ipynb'),
                         steps=[dict(slug='loop', status='todo', done=dict(outcome='right')), dict(slug='tools', status='todo'), dict(slug='memory', status='todo')]))
mine = walk_from_talk(wl, hw.id, ['memory', 'loop'])
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in mine.steps], ['memory', 'loop'])
test_eq((mine.get('parent'), for_talk(mine), mine.notebook, mine.chips), (None, False, dict(path='/u/k/a.ipynb'), ['file:/u/k/a.ipynb']))
assert mine.id != hw.id and not any('done' in s for s in mine.steps)
test_fail(lambda: walk_from_talk(wl, hw.id, ['gone']), contains='no idea')
```

#### The place that you used last

[`last_place`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#last_place)
says where Continue goes. It is the one function for the top bar, the
card on Today and the card of a course. A place is a step of a walk that
is not finished, or an open session with no walk. Each walk gives the
time that you used it last: the idea that you were on (`here`, which the
idea page writes), the newest idea that you read, or the start. A
session gives the time of its last change. The newest place wins. A side
walk counts as the step that opened it, so Continue goes back to the
paper. A side walk whose step is not there now (or that Leela opened) is
never a place. Only the newest `most` walks are read. The step is the
idea that you were on when it is not done, else the current step of the
walk.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L975"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def last_place(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, by:dict=None, most:int=10
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*The place that you used last, or None. A walk place has `walk`, `step`,
`title`, `done`, `total` and `course`; a session place has* `session`
and `title`. Each has `at`, the time that you used it.

### is_open

``` python
def is_open(
    s
)->bool:
```

*Whether filed session `s` is open: it has a log, it did not end, and it
has an answer or an open question.*

A walk that you read now wins over an older open session, and the
session wins when you use it after the walk.

``` python
pl2 = temp_learning(); pl2.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml'); pl2.put('Fusion', 'Join two lists.', 'ml')
two = [dict(slug='ranking', status='todo', check={}), dict(slug='fusion', status='todo', check={})]
now = time.time()
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='wa', title='Walk A', mode='walk', steps=two, started=now - 60, here=dict(step=1, at=now - 30)))
pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now - 600, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], open=True)
p = last_place(pl2)
test_eq((p.walk, p.step, p.title, p.done, p.total), ('wa', 1, 'Walk A', 0, 2))
pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], open=True)
test_eq((last_place(pl2).session, last_place(pl2).title), ('s1', 'Ranking'))
```

A side walk counts as the step that opened it. A finished walk, a walk
for a talk and an ended session are not places.

``` python
pl2.log_session('s1', 'open', start=now - 900, updated=now - 900, focus='ranking', concepts=['ranking'], log=[], ended=now - 900)
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='side', title='Side', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='fusion', status='todo', check={})], parent=dict(walk='wa', step=1, slug='fusion'), here=dict(step=0, at=now)))
test_eq((last_place(pl2).walk, last_place(pl2).step), ('wa', 1))
pl2.put_journey(dict(id='talk', title='Talk', mode='walk', steps=two, parent=dict(talk='t1', slide='s1'), here=dict(step=0, at=now + 9)))
test_eq(last_place(pl2).walk, 'wa')
for x in ('wa', 'side'): pl2.merge_journey(x, steps=[{**s, 'done': dict(outcome='solid', at=now)} for s in pl2.journey(x).steps])
test_eq(last_place(pl2), None)
```

A side walk with no parent step in a walk here is not a place: its walk
is gone, or Leela opened it.

``` python
pl3 = temp_learning(); pl3.put('Fusion', 'Join two lists.', 'ml')
one = [dict(slug='fusion', status='todo', check={})]
pl3.put_journey(dict(id='gone', title='Gone', mode='walk', steps=one, parent=dict(walk='nowhere', step=0), here=dict(step=0, at=now)))
pl3.put_journey(dict(id='lee', title='From Leela', mode='walk', steps=one, parent=dict(leela='lesson-1'), here=dict(step=0, at=now)))
test_eq(last_place(pl3), None)
```

#### An old path becomes a walk

Before 0.0.16 a goal could give a path: a walk with no `mode`, no
passage and no check of its own.
[`walk_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_path)
makes such a path a topic walk, one time, with the same id: the same
steps in the same order, each with a check, as
[`walk_from_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_from_topic)
does. A step that you marked known or skipped stays so, and an idea that
you learned is known.

The walk keeps the progress of the sessions of the path. A step with
answers is done or shaky. The newest open session is the sitting, with
its open question, which goes on the shelf of open questions
([`_keep_open`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#_keep_open)),
so the step shows it. `started` and `here` come from the sessions, so an
old path does not become the newest walk.

[`walk_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_path)
does not search the sources, so it is fast.
[`step_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#step_read)
finds the passage of one step when its idea opens.
[`walk_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_paths)
does it for each path, and gives the ids.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L1040"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>
