``` python
fw = lr.put_journey(dict(id='fw', title='Softmax', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug=s, status='todo', check=dict(way='words', kind='short', depth=2), **({'locked': True} if s in ('a', 'b') else {}))
                                                                 for s in ('a', 'softmax', 'b', 'c')]))
FX = dict(changes=[dict(op='remove', idea='a', why='x'), dict(op='harder', idea='b', why='x'), dict(op='move', idea='c', to=1, why='First the basics.'),
                   dict(op='easier', idea='softmax', why='Less to do.')])
f = Fake({'You redo the ideas of one learning walk': FX})
cs = propose(f, fw, {}, 'make the rest simpler', fix=True)
test_eq([(c.op, c.slug) for c in cs], [('move', 'c'), ('easier', 'softmax')])
assert 'idea a: a · check short, depth 2 · locked' in f.calls[0][0] and 'make the rest simpler' in f.calls[0][0]
```

With no words, Fix the rest still asks the tutor. The prompt then has no
words of the learner.

``` python
propose(f, fw, {}, '', fix=True)
assert '<source title="learner">' not in f.calls[-1][0]
```

The apply keeps the locked ideas byte for byte. A change to a locked
idea from an old proposal is left out too.

``` python
was = {s['slug']: json.dumps(s, sort_keys=True) for s in fw.steps if s.get('locked')}
w, rows = improve_walk(lr, f, 'fw', [*cs, AttrDict(op='remove', slug='b', name='', link='', to=None, why='')], fix=True)
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in w.steps], ['c', 'a', 'softmax', 'b'])
test_eq({s['slug']: json.dumps(s, sort_keys=True) for s in w.steps if s.get('locked')}, was)
test_eq((w.steps[2]['check']['depth'], rows[0].what), (1, 'Fixed the rest of the walk: 2 changes.'))
```

#### Make this walk again

The ⋯ menu of a walk has “Make this walk again”. It plans the walk again
from its own source, by the path that made it.
[`plan_again`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#plan_again)
picks that path:
[`journey_from_source`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#journey_from_source)
for a vault document (one of your notebooks is a
[`notebook_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#notebook_walk)),
[`journey_from_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#journey_from_sources)
for a link or for your sources, the ideas that a pasted text placed, and
[`walk_from_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_from_topic)
from the goal of a walk with no source. The new plan is a walk that the
vault does not keep: only its steps are used. `said(line)` tells what it
does now, and each line is a safe point for Stop.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2102"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### plan_again

``` python
def plan_again(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, j, sources:NoneType=None, who:str='', said:NoneType=None, asks:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*A new plan of walk `j` from its own source, by the path that made it,
with its `audience` and `no_code`; `asks` goes to the planner of a goal
walk. The vault does not keep the new walk; its steps are in the
result.*

[`merge_plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#merge_plan)
puts the new plan together with the old one. A locked idea stays as it
is, at its old place when it can. An idea that is in both plans keeps
what you did on it (`KEEP_RUN`: your outcome, your check, your read
time, your note, the ladder and the side walks), and its passage when
the new plan has none. Your answers and what you learned are in the
vault, so they stay too, as with Delete.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2119"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### merge_plan

``` python
def merge_plan(
    old:list, new:list, keep_read:bool=True
)->list:
```

*The steps of the new plan `new`, with each locked step of `old` as it
is, at its old place when it can. An idea in both keeps `KEEP_RUN`, and
its old passage when `keep_read` and the new plan has none.*

Two ideas are locked: `a` stays first and `d` stays at place 4. `b` is
in both plans, so it keeps its outcome. `c` is not in the new plan, so
it goes.

``` python
old = [dict(slug='a', locked=True, why='mine'), dict(slug='b', done=dict(outcome='solid'), why='old'), dict(slug='c'), dict(slug='d', locked=True)]
new = [dict(slug='x'), dict(slug='b', why='new'), dict(slug='a', why='new a'), dict(slug='y')]
out = merge_plan(old, new)
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in out], ['a', 'x', 'b', 'd', 'y'])
test_eq((out[0], out[2]['done'], out[2]['why']), (old[0], dict(outcome='solid'), 'new'))
```

[`replan_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#replan_walk)
does it all: the new plan, the merge, and one change in the history of
the walk, so one Undo takes it back. The new map of the walk goes on it
too. The line `said('Saving the new plan')` is the last safe point:
after Stop, the walk does not change.
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#plan) makes the
new plan; a test gives its own.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2137"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### replan_walk

``` python
def replan_walk(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, jid:str, sources:NoneType=None, who:str='', said:NoneType=None,
    plan:NoneType=None, asks:str='', **kw
)->tuple:
```

*Make the plan of walk `jid` again from its source
([`plan_again`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#plan_again)),
keep each locked idea
([`merge_plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#merge_plan)),
and keep it as one change with an Undo. Return `(walk, history)`.* `kw`
are new fields of the walk, such as `chips`, `audience` or `no_code`:
the new plan uses them, and the walk keeps them also when the new plan
has the same steps. They are part of the change, so Undo gives back
their old values. New `chips` also give a walk through its sources new
documents, and an old passage does not stay. `asks` goes to the planner.

A walk of four ideas with `a` locked. The new plan drops `c` and adds
`x`. One Undo gives back the old plan.

``` python
rw = lr.put_journey(dict(id='rw', title='Softmax', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug=s, status='todo', check=dict(way='words', kind='short', depth=2), **({'locked': True} if s == 'a' else {}))
                                                                 for s in ('a', 'softmax', 'b', 'c')]))
fresh = lambda lr, ask, j, *a: AttrDict(steps=[dict(slug=s, status='todo', check=dict(way='words', kind='short', depth=2)) for s in ('x', 'b', 'softmax')], map=dict(claim='New.', ideas=[]))
w, rows = replan_walk(lr, None, 'rw', plan=fresh)
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in w.steps], ['a', 'x', 'b', 'softmax'])
test_eq((rows[0].what, w.map['claim']), (REPLAN_WHAT, 'New.'))
undo_walk(lr, 'rw')
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in lr.journey('rw').steps], ['a', 'softmax', 'b', 'c'])
```

New sources and a new audience are part of the change. Undo gives back
the old ones, and a field that the walk did not have goes.

``` python
lr.merge_journey('rw', chips=['vault:old'])
w, rows = replan_walk(lr, None, 'rw', plan=fresh, chips=['vault:new'], audience='Managers')
test_eq((w.chips, w.audience), (['vault:new'], 'Managers'))
undo_walk(lr, 'rw')
test_eq((lr.journey('rw').chips, 'audience' in lr.journey('rw')), (['vault:old'], False))
```

A Stop before the save changes nothing.

``` python
def stopper(line):
    if line == 'Saving the new plan': raise RuntimeError('stopped')
try: replan_walk(lr, None, 'rw', said=stopper, plan=fresh); raise AssertionError('no stop')
except RuntimeError: pass
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in lr.journey('rw').steps], ['a', 'softmax', 'b', 'c'])
```

New fields of the walk, such as other `chips`, an `audience` or
`no_code`, go to the new plan. The walk keeps them also when the new
plan has the same steps. `asks` goes to the planner and is not kept.

``` python
seen = []
spy = lambda lr, ask, j, *a: (seen.append((j.get('chips'), j.get('audience'), j.get('no_code'), a[-1])), fresh(lr, ask, j))[1]
w, _ = replan_walk(lr, None, 'rw', plan=spy, asks='No maths.', chips=['file:/x/notes.md'], audience='people who do not write code', no_code=True)
test_eq(seen, [(['file:/x/notes.md'], 'people who do not write code', True, 'No maths.')])
test_eq((w.chips, w.audience, w.no_code, 'asks' in w), (['file:/x/notes.md'], 'people who do not write code', True, False))
w.chips, w.audience, w.no_code
```

The new plan can have the same steps. The walk still keeps the new
fields, and the change in its history has only their old values, for its
Undo.

``` python
lr.merge_journey('rw', audience='', no_code=False)
w, rows = replan_walk(lr, None, 'rw', plan=fresh, audience='busy managers', no_code=True)
test_eq((rows[0].was, rows[0].before == [dict(s) for s in w.steps]), ({'audience': '', 'no_code': False}, True))   # the steps are the same: the change keeps only the old fields
test_eq((w.audience, w.no_code), ('busy managers', True))
test_eq((lr.journey('rw').audience, lr.journey('rw').no_code), ('busy managers', True))
```

With `no_code`, a check is never code: a step that the plan marks as a
notebook, or an idea whose only way is code, gets a check in a text way.

``` python
ck = [_check(lr, AttrDict(slug='x', ways=['code']), kind='notebook', no_code=True), _check(lr, AttrDict(slug='x', ways=['code']), True, no_code=True)]
test_eq([c.kind for c in ck], ['short', 'short'])
test_eq(_check(lr, AttrDict(slug='x', ways=['code']), kind='notebook').kind, 'notebook')   # without it, the plan's notebook stays
ck
```

## Courses

A course to your goal: its sources, its stages, where you are, what
comes next and why. The module is `abhyasa.path`.

A goal such as “fine-tune my own diffusion model to make Indian comics”
needs more than one walk. A **course** is all that abhyasa has for one
goal: its sources, its **stages** (one walk each), and your answers to
“what do you know already?”.

The course keeps only what abhyasa cannot get again from other records.
“You are here”, “next and why” and “what stands between you and the
goal” come from the walks, the concepts and the Leela results each time
that you ask. So each fact has one place, and no field gets old.

This module has no web page. The `course` block shows it.

- **The record**: one vault document of kind `course` on the learning
  shelf, as a walk is.
- **Join**: a goal walk makes a course, or joins the course of the same
  goal, as its first stage.
- **Where you start**: a few short questions from the model. Your
  answers set where the course starts and how many stages it has.
- **Stages**: the planner gives the stages. The next stage is built when
  the current one is 60% done, or when you open it.
- **The state**:
  [`course_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#course_state)
  and
  [`next_up`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#next_up),
  with eight ordered rules, each with a one-line reason.

Import the shelf, the learner model, the walk engine, the JSON call of
the model and the guard for text that leaves the Mac.

### The limits

`GROW_AT` is the share of a stage that you finish before abhyasa builds
the next stage. `UNCLEAR` is the time in which two boards or explainers
on one idea make it unclear. A course keeps at most `ASKS_MOST` asks,
the newest.

### The record

A course is one document of kind `course` on the learning shelf. Its
fields:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>field</th>
<th>meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>id</code>, <code>goal</code>, <code>title</code>,
<code>subject</code>, <code>makes</code></td>
<td>the goal is your words, as you typed them</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sources</code></td>
<td><code>{id, kind, root, count, status, why}</code> for each chip: <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#ready"><code>ready</code></a>,
<code>filing</code> or <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed"><code>failed</code></a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>stages</code></td>
<td><code>{key, name, makes, ideas, foundation, skip_if, short, walk, status}</code>
in order: <code>planned</code>, <code>building</code>, <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#ready"><code>ready</code></a>
or <code>skipped</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>level</code></td>
<td><code>{at, qs: [{key, q, idea, answer, by}]}</code>: the questions
of “where do you start”, and your answers</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>here</code></td>
<td><code>{walk, step, slug, at}</code>: the last idea that you
opened</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>asks</code></td>
<td><code>{at, where, said, slug, kind, ref, outcome}</code>: boards,
explainers and demos that you asked for</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>proposal</code></td>
<td>ideas that a new source adds, not applied yet</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>v</code></td>

</tr>
</tbody>

[`new_course`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#new_course)

``` python
from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
c0 = lr.put_course(new_course('Make  a  comic', title='Comics'))
test_eq((c0.goal, c0.v, lr.courses().attrgot('id')), ('Make a comic', 1, [c0.id]))
test_eq(lr.merge_course(c0.id, makes='One panel').v, 2)
test_eq(lr.change_course(c0.id, lambda c: c.stages.append(dict(key='s1', name='One'))).stages[0]['name'], 'One')
lr.drop_course(c0.id); test_eq(lr.courses(), [])
```

### A goal walk joins a course

A walk that you plan from a goal (`from_goal` in the walk block) is a
**goal walk**: a walk with a goal, no source document, no parent, and
not for a talk.
[`join_course`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#join_course)
gives it a course: the course of the same goal, else a new one. The walk
is a stage of the course, and the walk knows its course (`course`,
`stage`).

[`chip_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#chip_sources)
makes the source rows from the chips of the walk. A chip that did not
file is
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed),
with the line that the walk kept.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2254"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
ls_ = temp_learning()
did = ls_.vault.put('The alliance system tied the powers of Europe together.', 'https://ex.org/alliances', 'web', title='Polarization of Europe')['doc_id']
rows = [dict(id='link:https://ex.org/alliances', status='failed', why='abhyasa could not file it.', root='https://ex.org/alliances'),
        dict(id=f'doc:{did}', status='failed', why='', root=did), dict(id='link:https://ex.org/none', status='failed', why='abhyasa could not file it.', root='x')]
got = source_rows(ls_, rows)
test_eq([(r['status'], r['root'], r['kind']) for r in got[:1]], [('ready', 'Polarization of Europe', 'a document')])   # the page and its document are one row
test_eq((len(got), got[0]['page'], got[1]['status'], got[1]['why']), (2, 'https://ex.org/alliances', 'unknown', UNKNOWN))
```

### join_course

``` python
def join_course(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, j
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*The course of goal walk `j` (a walk or its id): its own, else the
course of the same goal, else a new one. The walk becomes a stage. None
for a walk that is not a goal walk.*

A small goal walk, as the Start box makes it: two chips, and the clone
of one failed.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
for n, pre in (('Noise', []), ('Denoise', ['noise']), ('Sample', ['denoise'])): lr.put(n, f'{n} a picture.', 'ml', prereqs=pre)
def goal_walk(lr, jid='gw', goal='Fine-tune diffusion for comics', slugs=('noise', 'denoise', 'sample'), **kw):
    return lr.put_journey(dict(id=jid, title='Diffusion for comics', goal=goal, mode='walk', source=None, started=None, created=1.,
                               steps=[dict(slug=s, status='todo', check=dict(way='words', kind='short', depth=2)) for s in slugs],
                               chips=['folder:/x/course22p2', 'gh:huggingface/diffusers'], chip_counts={'folder:/x/course22p2': 44},
                               notes=['abhyasa could not clone huggingface/diffusers.'], **kw))
gw = goal_walk(lr)
```

The walk joins a new course as stage `s1`. The failed clone is a
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed)
source with its line. A second call gives the same course.

``` python
c = join_course(lr, gw)
test_eq([(s['key'], s['walk'], s['status']) for s in c.stages], [('s1', 'gw', 'ready')])
test_eq([(s['root'], s['status']) for s in c.sources], [('course22p2', 'ready'), ('huggingface/diffusers', 'failed')])
test_eq(c.sources[1]['why'], 'abhyasa could not clone huggingface/diffusers.')
test_eq((lr.journey('gw').course, lr.journey('gw').stage), (c.id, 's1'))
test_eq(join_course(lr, 'gw').id, c.id); test_eq(len(lr.courses()), 1); test_eq(course_of(lr, 'gw').id, c.id)
```

A second goal walk with the same goal (case and spaces do not count)
joins the same course as stage `s2`. A side walk joins nothing.

``` python
goal_walk(lr, 'gw2', goal='fine-tune  Diffusion for comics')
test_eq(join_course(lr, 'gw2').stages[-1]['key'], 's2'); test_eq(len(lr.courses()), 1)
lr.put_journey(dict(id='side', title='S', goal='x', mode='walk', source=None, parent=dict(walk='gw', step=0), steps=[]))
test_is(join_course(lr, 'side'), None)
```

[`ensure_courses`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#ensure_courses)
gives a course to an older goal walk that has none, one time.

``` python
l2 = temp_learning(); l2.put('Noise', 'n', 'ml'); goal_walk(l2, slugs=('noise',))
test_eq(len(ensure_courses(l2)), 1); test_eq(ensure_courses(l2), [])
```

### Where do you start

Before abhyasa plans the stages, it asks what you know already: a few
short questions, such as “Do you know how a neural network learns?”. You
answer each with yes, a little, or no, by a tap or by voice. The model
writes the questions from the goal. An idea that you learned already (a
concept at the learned depth) gets the answer yes from the shelf, and
abhyasa does not ask it.

The prompt goes through the guard of ramabana
([`guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#guard)), as
the other calls do, so no secret or personal data leaves the Mac.

### ask_level

``` python
def ask_level(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, cid:str, who:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Write the questions of “where do you start” for course `cid` and keep
them on it. Older answers go.*

A fake model writes three questions. You learned Noise already, so its
question has the answer yes from the shelf.

``` python
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
LEVEL = dict(questions=[dict(q='Do you know how a neural network learns?', idea='How a neural network learns'),
                        dict(q='Do you know what noise is?', idea='Noise'), dict(q='Have you used diffusers?', idea='The diffusers library')])
lr.update('noise', floor=4, seen=1)
ask = Fake({'You find out what one learner knows': LEVEL})
c = ask_level(lr, ask, c.id)
test_eq([(q['key'], q['answer'], q['by']) for q in c.level['qs']], [('q1', None, ''), ('q2', 'yes', 'shelf'), ('q3', None, '')])
test_eq(level_done(c), False)
c = answer_level(lr, c.id, 'q1', 'no, never'); c = answer_level(lr, c.id, 'q3', 'a little')
test_eq((c.level['qs'][0]['answer'], level_done(c)), ('no', True))
test_fail(lambda: answer_level(lr, c.id, 'q1', 'banana'), contains='yes, a little, or no')
```

### Stages

[`plan_stages`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#plan_stages)
asks the planner for the stages of the course. It gives the planner your
answers and the stages that have a walk. The planner marks a stage that
teaches the basics as `foundation`, with `skip_if`: the question that
makes it not needed.

Then the rules decide, not the model:

- A foundation stage whose question you answered **yes** is `skipped`.
  It shows, but it counts nothing.
- A foundation stage whose question you answered **a little** is
  `short`: a refresher of 3 or 4 ideas.
- A foundation stage comes before the stages that have a walk. The other
  new stages come after them.
- A stage that has a walk stays as it is, and so does a locked stage
  (`locked: True`). The other stages are planned again each time.
- Fix the rest (`fix=True`) plans again each stage that you did not lock
  or start. A locked stage stays, and so does a stage whose walk you
  started (`started`, or a step done or shaky): a replan has no Undo, so
  it never drops your progress. A stage with a walk that you did not
  start leaves the course; its walk stays on Home.
  [`fix_count`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#fix_count)
  counts the stages that Fix the rest plans again.

So the answers set where the course starts and how many stages it has.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2383"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### lock_stage

``` python
def lock_stage(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, cid:str, key:str, on:bool=True
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Lock stage `key` of course `cid`, or unlock it. A stage that is not
there raises `KeyError`.*

A fake planner gives three stages for the diffusion goal. The first
teaches how a neural network learns, and is skipped when you answer yes
to `q1`.

``` python
STAGES = dict(title='Diffusion for comics', makes='a LoRA in your comic style', stages=[
    dict(name='How a neural network learns', makes='a small net that learns', ideas=['Gradient descent', 'Loss'], foundation=True, skip_if='q1'),
    dict(name='Diffusion for comics', makes='x', ideas=[]),   # the stage that has a walk: not again
    dict(name='Your comic data', makes='captions.jsonl', ideas=['Captions', 'Image size'])])
ask = Fake({'You find out what one learner knows': LEVEL, 'You plan a course to one learner': STAGES})
def course_with(answer):
    l = temp_learning(); l.put('Noise', 'n', 'ml'); goal_walk(l, slugs=('noise',))
    c = join_course(l, 'gw'); ask_level(l, ask, c.id)
    for k in ('q1', 'q2', 'q3'): answer_level(l, c.id, k, answer)
    return l, plan_stages(l, ask, c.id)
```

A learner who does **not** know how a neural network learns gets the
foundation stage first, before the goal walk.

``` python
l, c = course_with('no')
test_eq([(s['name'], s['status']) for s in c.stages], [('How a neural network learns', 'planned'), ('Diffusion for comics', 'ready'), ('Your comic data', 'planned')])
test_eq(c.makes, 'a LoRA in your comic style')
```

A learner who knows it skips the foundation stage. A learner who knows
it a little gets a short one.

``` python
l, c = course_with('yes')
test_eq([(s['name'], s['status']) for s in c.stages][0], ('How a neural network learns', 'skipped'))
test_eq(c.stages[0]['why'], 'You know it: How a neural network learns')
test_eq(course_with('some')[1].stages[0]['short'], True)
```

Lock the third stage, then Fix the rest. The locked stage stays as it
was, byte for byte, and the planner sees it. The goal walk stage is not
locked, so it leaves the course, and a new stage takes the place of the
old plan. Its key is new.

``` python
l, c = course_with('no')
c = lock_stage(l, c.id, c.stages[2]['key']); was = json.dumps(c.stages[2], sort_keys=True)
fx = Fake({'You plan a course to one learner': dict(title='x', makes='x', stages=[dict(name='Noise schedules', makes='a schedule', ideas=['Beta'])])})
c2 = plan_stages(l, fx, c.id, fix=True)
test_eq([s['name'] for s in c2.stages], ['Your comic data', 'Noise schedules'])
test_eq((json.dumps(c2.stages[0], sort_keys=True), c2.stages[1]['key']), (was, 's4'))
assert 'Your comic data' in fx.calls[-1][0] and course_of(l, 'gw') is None
```

Unlock it, and a plain replan plans it again.

``` python
c = lock_stage(l, c.id, c2.stages[0]['key'], on=False)
test_eq([s['name'] for s in plan_stages(l, fx, c.id).stages], ['Noise schedules'])
```

A stage whose walk you started stays after Fix the rest, as if it were
locked. A stage that you never started is planned again.
[`fix_count`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#fix_count)
counts only that one.

``` python
l, c = course_with('no'); l.merge_journey('gw', started=time.time())
test_eq(fix_count(l, l.course(c.id)), 2)
c2 = plan_stages(l, fx, c.id, fix=True)
test_eq([s['name'] for s in c2.stages], ['Diffusion for comics', 'Noise schedules'])
test_eq((c2.stages[0]['walk'], fix_count(l, c2)), ('gw', 1))
```

### Build a stage

[`build_stage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#build_stage)
makes the walk of one planned stage. It also makes the walk of a skipped
stage when you ask for it, and the stage stays skipped if this fails.
The planner gets a brief: the goal, the stage, its ideas, and the ideas
of the earlier stages, which it leaves out. A step on a concept of an
earlier stage goes, so a stage never asks an idea again. The walk knows
its course and stage, and it reads the sources of the course.

[`due_stage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#due_stage)
says which stage to build now: the current stage when it has no walk, or
the next stage when the current one is `GROW_AT` (60%) done.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2467"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

A skipped stage stays `skipped` until its walk is made: a failure does

### stage_brief

``` python
def stage_brief(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, c, st
)->str:
```

*The goal for the planner of stage `st` of course `c`.*

A fake planner gives the walk of the data stage. It names Noise again,
which stage 1 has, so that step goes.

``` python
PLAN = dict(title='Data', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Noise', statement='n', why='w'), dict(name='Captions', statement='Words for each picture.', why='w'),
                                               dict(name='Image size', statement='An image is 512 pixels.', why='w')])
ask.rules['You plan a learning path'] = PLAN
l, c = course_with('yes')
data = first(s for s in c.stages if s['name'] == 'Your comic data')
sj = build_stage(l, ask, c.id, data['key'])
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in sj.steps], ['captions', 'image-size'])
test_eq((sj.course, sj.stage, sj.goal, sj.title), (c.id, data['key'], c.goal, 'Your comic data'))
test_eq(first(s for s in l.course(c.id).stages if s['key'] == data['key'])['status'], 'ready')
test_eq(build_stage(l, ask, c.id, data['key']).id, sj.id)   # a second call gives the same walk
test_is('Earlier stages teach these ideas, so leave them out: Noise.' in stage_brief(l, c, data), True)
```

#### Your data on a course

[`add_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#add_data)
keeps a folder on the course as your data, with a note. abhyasa does not
file it and does not learn from it: the exercises run on it. The walks
of the stages keep the same list, so the notebook of each step in Leela
gets it. A walk that a stage makes later gets it from
[`build_stage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#build_stage).
[`drop_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#drop_data)
removes one folder from the course and its walks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2502"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, cid:str, path:str

```

*Remove the data folder `path` from course `cid` and its walks. The
folder stays on the disk.*

### add_data

``` python
def add_data(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, cid:str, path, note:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Keep the folder `path` with `note` on course `cid` and its walks as
your data. A `ValueError` says in one line why abhyasa cannot.*

A folder added as data is on the course and on its walk. The walk that a
stage makes after that keeps it, and the planner sees it in the data
list, with a listing of the folder. A path that is not a folder is
refused.
[`drop_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#drop_data)
removes it from the course and from each walk.

``` python
home, old = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(), os.environ['HOME']
os.environ['HOME'] = str(home)
try:
    (home/'episodes').mkdir(); (home/'episodes'/'episodes.json').write_text('{}')
    l2, c2 = course_with('yes')
    c2 = add_data(l2, c2.id, str(home/'episodes'), 'The episodes that my scenarios run on.')
    with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, 'no folder'): add_data(l2, c2.id, '~/nothing')
    j2 = build_stage(l2, ask, c2.id, first(s for s in c2.stages if s['name'] == 'Your comic data')['key'])
finally: os.environ['HOME'] = old
mine = [dict(path='~/episodes', note='The episodes that my scenarios run on.')]
test_eq((c2.data, l2.journey('gw').data, j2.data), (mine, mine, mine))
assert '- EPISODES: The episodes that my scenarios run on. It holds: episodes.json.' in first(p for p, sp in reversed(ask.calls) if 'You plan a learning path' in p + sp)
c2 = drop_data(l2, c2.id, '~/episodes')
test_eq((c2.data, l2.journey('gw').data, l2.journey(j2.id).data), ([], [], []))
```

#### Set the folder of one data name

A notebook step names its data, as EPISODES.
[`name_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#name_data)
keeps the folder that you pick under Your data with that name: on the
course of the walk and its walks, else on the walk. Then
[`fill_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#fill_data)
puts the path in the notebook spec of each step of those walks that
names it, so the spec that Leela reads has the path. A second folder for
the same name takes the place of the first.

### fill_data

``` python
def fill_data(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Walk `jid` with its data folders in the notebook spec of each of its
steps, so the spec that Leela reads has each path that you set.*

Step 0 of the course walk needs EPISODES. After
[`name_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#name_data),
the course, the walk and the spec of the step have the folder, and
nothing is missing. A path outside the home folder gives one plain
reason:

``` python
home, old = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(), os.environ['HOME']
os.environ['HOME'] = str(home)
try:
    (home/'comics').mkdir()
    l3, c3 = course_with('yes')
    l3.walk_step('gw', 0, nb=dict(data=[dict(name='EPISODES', path='', what='Text of the comic episodes.', need=True)]))
    test_eq([d['name'] for d in missing_data(l3.journey('gw'))], ['EPISODES'])
    row = name_data(l3, 'gw', 'EPISODES', str(home/'comics'), 'Text of the comic episodes.')
    with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, 'abhyasa cannot use this folder: the path is not in your home folder.'): name_data(l3, 'gw', 'IMAGES', '/etc')
finally: os.environ['HOME'] = old
test_eq(row, dict(path='~/comics', note='Text of the comic episodes.', name='EPISODES'))
test_eq((l3.course(c3.id).data, l3.journey('gw').data), ([row], [row]))
test_eq(l3.journey('gw').steps[0]['nb']['data'][0]['path'], '~/comics')
test_eq(missing_data(l3.journey('gw')), [])
```

#### One name for one folder in the stored specs

[`same_names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#same_names)
gives one name to one folder only in a new spec. A spec that is already
stored can still use two names for the same data, as IMAGES in one step
and COMIC_IMAGES in another.
[`join_names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#join_names)
joins them: entries whose `what` is the same after case and punctuation
are removed get one name. That name is the name under Your data when one
of them has it, else the first name that the walk uses. Only the names
change, in the data, the task, the stub, `run.say` and `run.predict`,
and only as whole words.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2547"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*Give one name to one folder in the stored notebook specs of walk `jid`
([`join_names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#join_names)),
and log each change. Each step that names the folder* then has its path
from Your data
([`fill_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#fill_data)).
The place of the walk in the list stays. Gives the changes
`[(step, old, new)]`.

### join_names

``` python
def join_names(
    j
)->tuple:
```

*Walk `j` with one data name for each `what` in the notebook specs of
its steps, and the changes `[(step, old, new)]`.* The name is the name
under Your data (`j.data`) when an entry has it, else the first name
used. With no change, `j` itself.

Two stored specs name the same comic images IMAGES and COMIC_IMAGES.
After the join, both use IMAGES, the first name, also in the task and
the run. The missing-data line asks for one folder:

``` python
jl = temp_learning()
imgs = lambda n: dict(name=n, path='', what='Indian comic page or panel images.', need=True)
jl.put_journey(dict(id='cw', title='Comics', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='loss', nb=dict(task='Load IMAGES.', data=[imgs('IMAGES')])),
    dict(slug='fit', nb=dict(task='Load COMIC_IMAGES.', stub='COMIC_IMAGES_2 = 1', data=[imgs('COMIC_IMAGES')], run=dict(say='Read COMIC_IMAGES.', predict='')))]))
test_eq([d['name'] for d in missing_data(jl.journey('cw'))], ['IMAGES', 'COMIC_IMAGES'])
test_eq(jl.join_data_names('cw'), [(1, 'COMIC_IMAGES', 'IMAGES')])
s1 = jl.journey('cw').steps[1]['nb']
test_eq((s1['task'], s1['stub'], s1['run']['say'], s1['data'][0]['what']), ('Load IMAGES.', 'COMIC_IMAGES_2 = 1', 'Read IMAGES.', 'Indian comic page or panel images.'))
test_eq([data_line(d) for d in missing_data(jl.journey('cw'))], ['IMAGES: Indian comic page or panel images.'])
```

A second join changes nothing. When Your data has a folder named
COMIC_IMAGES, that name wins, and each step gets its path:

``` python
test_eq(jl.join_data_names('cw'), [])
jl.put_journey(dict(id='cy', title='Comics', mode='walk', data=[dict(path='~/comics', note='', name='COMIC_IMAGES')],
                    steps=[dict(slug='loss', nb=dict(task='Load IMAGES.', data=[imgs('IMAGES')])), dict(slug='fit', nb=dict(data=[imgs('COMIC_IMAGES')]))]))
test_eq(jl.join_data_names('cy'), [(0, 'IMAGES', 'COMIC_IMAGES')])
test_eq([(s['nb']['task'] if 'task' in s['nb'] else '', [(d['name'], d['path']) for d in s['nb']['data']]) for s in jl.journey('cy').steps],
        [('Load COMIC_IMAGES.', [('COMIC_IMAGES', '~/comics')]), ('', [('COMIC_IMAGES', '~/comics')])])
test_eq(missing_data(jl.journey('cy')), [])
```

A skipped stage stays skipped when its build fails. Here the planner
gives only Noise again, so the stage gets no new ideas.

``` python
sl, sc = course_with('yes')
k0 = sc.stages[0]['key']
ask.rules['You plan a learning path'] = dict(title='Nets', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Noise', statement='n', why='w')])
test_fail(lambda: build_stage(sl, ask, sc.id, k0), contains='no new ideas')
test_eq({k: sl.course(sc.id).stages[0][k] for k in ('status', 'why')}, dict(status='skipped', why='You know it: How a neural network learns'))
```

When the build of a skipped stage works, the stage gets its walk and is
ready.

``` python
ask.rules['You plan a learning path'] = dict(title='Nets', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Loss', statement='How wrong the net is.', why='w')])
test_eq((build_stage(sl, ask, sc.id, k0).stage, sl.course(sc.id).stages[0]['status']), (k0, 'ready'))
ask.rules['You plan a learning path'] = PLAN
```

### The state of a course

[`stage_rows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#stage_rows)
gives each stage with its walk, its counts and one state word: `done`,
[`ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#ready) (it
has a walk, and ideas to learn), `planned`, `building`, `skipped`, or
`known`. A planned stage whose ideas you learned in the meantime is
`known`: the plan changes when what you show in checks changes. The
**current stage** is the first stage that is
[`ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#ready),
`planned` or `building`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2578"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### due_stage

``` python
def due_stage(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, c, rows:NoneType=None
)->str | None:
```

*The key of the stage to build now: the current stage when it has no
walk, else the next planned stage when the current one is `GROW_AT`
done.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2563"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### stage_rows

``` python
def stage_rows(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, c, by:dict=None
)->list:
```

*Each stage of course `c` with `n`, its walk `j`, its
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#walk_state)
`ws`, `done`, `total` and `state`.*

The data stage has a walk now. Stage 1 is skipped. Stage 2 (the goal
walk) is current and less than 60% done, so
[`due_stage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#due_stage)
names nothing to build.

``` python
rows = stage_rows(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq([(r.n, r.state) for r in rows], [(1, 'skipped'), (2, 'ready'), (3, 'ready')])
test_eq(due_stage(l, l.course(c.id)), None)
```

In the course of a learner who said no, the foundation stage is current
and has no walk, so it is due at once. A planned stage whose ideas you
learned is `known`.

``` python
l, c = course_with('no')
test_eq(due_stage(l, c), 's2')
for n in ('Gradient descent', 'Loss'): l.put(n, n, 'ml'); l.update(l.concepts().filter(lambda x: x.name == n)[0].slug, floor=4, seen=1)
test_eq(stage_rows(l, c)[0].state, 'known'); test_eq(due_stage(l, c), None)
```

### What to learn next, and why

[`next_up`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#next_up)
gives one thing to do and one reason. The first rule that gives a thing
wins:

<table>

<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>#</th>
<th>rule</th>
<th>reason</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>Leela filed a failed check on an idea of the current stage</td>
<td>“Your notebook did not pass. Look at the error first.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>A review is due for an idea that the current stage needs, and its
recall is under <code>review.fading</code></td>
<td>“Review Softmax first. The next idea needs it, and you start to
forget it.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3</td>
<td>You asked about an idea of the stage two or more times in two days
(boards, explainers), with no right check since</td>
<td>“You asked about alpha bar two times. Check it now.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>The next idea is ready: you know the ideas that it needs</td>
<td>“Next: Add noise at step t. You know the ideas that it needs.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5</td>
<td>The next idea is not ready</td>

</tr>
<tr>

needs</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>7</td>
<td>The current stage has no walk yet</td>
<td>“Stage 3 is next: Your comic data. It makes captions.jsonl.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8</td>
<td>All stages are done</td>
<td>“You reached your goal.”</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Rules for all: only one review before a new idea, so the course moves (a
review since the last idea that you finished turns rule 2 off). A demo
or an explainer never counts as learned. When you opened an idea that is
not the first one to learn, it wins once, and the reason says “You
opened this idea last, so you go on from it.”

`go` says where the button goes: `{kind: 'step', walk, step}`,
`{kind: 'review', slug}`, `{kind: 'stage', key}` or `{kind: 'done'}`.
The block makes the link.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2641"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### next_up

``` python
def next_up(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, c, rows:NoneType=None, by:dict=None, now:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The one thing to do next in course `c`: `rule`, `why` (one line),
`slug`, `name`, `stage` and `go`.*

#### Each rule, with a small course

`fixture` makes a course with one goal walk of three ideas: Noise, then
Denoise (it needs Noise), then Sample (it needs Denoise). `done(i)`
marks idea `i` done, with its concept at depth 4.

``` python
def fixture():
    l = temp_learning()
    for n, pre in (('Noise', []), ('Denoise', ['noise']), ('Sample', ['denoise'])): l.put(n, f'{n} a picture.', 'ml', prereqs=pre)
    goal_walk(l); c = join_course(l, 'gw')
    return l, c
def done(l, i, at=None):
    slug = l.journey('gw').steps[i]['slug']
    l.walk_step('gw', i, done=dict(outcome='solid', at=at or time.time())); l.update(slug, floor=4, seen=1, last=time.time(), stability=5., due=time.time() + 5 * 86400)
```

**Rule 4.** Two ideas are done, so you are at idea 3, and you know what
it needs.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); done(l, 1)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.slug, nx.go), (4, 'sample', dict(kind='step', walk='gw', step=2)))
test_eq(nx.why, 'Next: Sample. You know the ideas that it needs.')
```

**Rule 4, you chose it.** You opened idea 3 while idea 2 is still to
learn. Your pick wins, with its reason.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); l.update('denoise', floor=3)   # Denoise is ready to build on, but not learned
l.merge_course(c.id, here=dict(walk='gw', step=2, slug='sample', at=time.time()))
test_eq((next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).slug, next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).why), ('sample', 'You opened this idea last, so you go on from it.'))
```

**Rule 5.** Nothing is done, and idea 2 is next when you skip idea 1:
Denoise needs Noise, which you do not know.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); l.walk_step('gw', 0, done=dict(outcome='skipped', at=time.time()))
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.slug, nx.why), (5, 'denoise', 'Next: Noise first. Denoise needs it.'))
```

**Rule 1.** Leela filed a failed check for idea 3. That comes first.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); done(l, 1)
l.record('sample', 'Run the tests', correct=False, kind='code', app='leela', walk='gw', step=2)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.go['step'], nx.why), (1, 2, 'Your notebook did not pass. Look at the error first.'))
```

**Rule 2.** Denoise is done, Sample needs it, and its review is due with
a low recall. After one review, the course moves on.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0, at=time.time() - 20 * 86400); done(l, 1, at=time.time() - 20 * 86400)
l.update('denoise', last=time.time() - 30 * 86400, stability=1., due=time.time() - 86400)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.go, nx.why), (2, dict(kind='review', slug='denoise'), 'Review Denoise first. The next idea needs it, and you start to forget it.'))
l.record('denoise', 'What does denoise do?', correct=True)
test_eq(next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).rule, 4)
```

[`add_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#add_ask)
keeps one ask on the course: a board of the screen guide, an explainer,
a demo or a notebook. It keeps only the words that you said, the idea
and the time, never the page.

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### add_ask

``` python
def add_ask(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, cid:str, where:str, slug:str, kind:str, said:str='', ref:str='', outcome:str='',
    at:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Keep one ask on course `cid`: `where` (walk, session or guide), the
idea `slug`, its `kind`, your words
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said). At most
`ASKS_MOST`, the newest.*

**Rule 3.** You asked the screen guide about idea 3 two times. A right
check after the last ask clears it.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); done(l, 1)
for _ in range(2): add_ask(l, c.id, 'guide', 'sample', 'board', said='what is sampling?', at=time.time() - 60)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.why), (3, 'You asked about Sample two times. Check it now.'))
l.record('sample', 'Sample one picture', correct=True)
test_eq(next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).rule, 4)
test_fail(lambda: add_ask(l, c.id, 'guide', 'sample', 'page'), contains='kind of ask')
```

**Rules 6, 7 and 8.** With the goal walk done and a planned stage after
it, the next stage comes, after a weak idea that it needs. With no stage
left, you reached your goal.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); [done(l, i) for i in range(3)]
l.change_course(c.id, lambda c: c.stages.append(dict(key='s2', name='Your comic data', makes='captions.jsonl', ideas=['Sample', 'Captions'], walk=None, status='planned')))
test_eq(next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).why, 'Stage 2 is next: Your comic data. It makes captions.jsonl.')
l.update('sample', misses=2)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id)); test_eq((nx.rule, nx.why), (6, 'Practice Sample. Stage 2 builds on it.'))
l.change_course(c.id, lambda c: c.stages.pop())
test_eq(next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).why, 'You reached your goal.')
```

#### What stands between you and the goal

[`blocking`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#blocking)
gives the rows, in this order, each with a line and one action:

- **idea**: the ideas still to learn in the stages that are not
  finished;
- **weak**: an idea that you learned, that is weak now, and that a stage
  still to do needs;
- **notebook**: notebook ideas with no passed check from Leela;
- **setup**: Leela is not running (when the block knows it,
  `leela=False`), or a notebook has no folder for its data (one row for
  each data name, with the entry `data` and its `walk`, so the page can
  show a folder setter);
- **source**: a source that failed or still files, ideas that research
  still looks for, and a stage with no passage for half of its ideas.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2677"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### blocking

``` python
def blocking(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, c, rows:NoneType=None, by:dict=None, leela:bool=None, now:float=None
)->list:
```

*The rows of “what stands between you and the goal”:
`{kind, line, act, go}`, in the order of the kinds.*

A failed clone shows a `source` row. A notebook idea with Leela off
shows a `notebook` row and a `setup` row, and its empty data folder a
second `setup` row.

``` python
l, c = fixture()
l.walk_slug('gw', 'sample', check=dict(way='code', kind='notebook', depth=4), nb=dict(data=[dict(name='COMICS', what='Your comic images.', path='')]))
bs = blocking(l, l.course(c.id), leela=False)
test_eq([b.kind for b in bs], ['idea', 'notebook', 'setup', 'setup', 'source', 'source'])
test_eq(bs[0].line, '3 ideas: Noise, Denoise, Sample.')
test_eq([b.line for b in bs[1:5]], ['1 notebook to run in Leela: Sample.', 'Leela is not running. Start Leela to run the notebooks.',
                                    'COMICS: your comic images.', 'abhyasa could not clone huggingface/diffusers.'])
test_eq(bs[5].line, 'Stage 1: 3 ideas have no source yet.')
test_eq((bs[3].data, bs[3].walk), (dict(name='COMICS', what='Your comic images.'), 'gw'))
```

#### [`course_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#course_state)

[`course_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#course_state)
puts it together for the page, with no write: the course, the stages,
the current stage, “you are here”, the counts over all stages (a planned
stage counts by its plan), next and why, the blocking rows, what you
made in Leela, and `finished`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2705"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### course_state

``` python
def course_state(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, cid:str, leela:bool=None, now:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*Where you are in course `cid`, what comes next and why, and what stands
between you and the goal. It writes nothing. None for an unknown
course.*

The state of the fixture after two ideas: you are at idea 3 of 3 in
stage 1, and two of three ideas are done.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); done(l, 1)
st = course_state(l, c.id)
test_eq((st.here.n, st.here.of, st.here.stage, st.here.name), (3, 3, 1, 'Sample'))
test_eq((st.done, st.total, st.next.rule, st.finished), (2, 3, 4, False))
done(l, 2); test_eq(course_state(l, c.id).finished, True)
test_is(course_state(l, 'none'), None)
```

### Known ideas

An idea that you learned in a session or in another walk counts: it
shows “known (learned elsewhere)”, it asks nothing, and its review comes
when it is due. Here you learn Denoise in a session. The course counts
it, and “you are here” goes past it.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0)
l.update('denoise', floor=4, seen=1)   # a session closed Denoise at depth 4
st = course_state(l, c.id)
test_eq([s.dot for s in st.stages[0].ws.steps], ['done', 'known', 'now'])
test_eq((st.stages[0].ws.steps[1].elsewhere, st.done, st.here.name), (True, 2, 'Sample'))
```

A new goal walk marks an idea that you learned as `known` when it is
made, so it never asks it.

``` python
l = temp_learning(); l.put('Noise', 'n', 'ml'); l.update('noise', floor=4, seen=1)
wj = walk_from_topic(l, Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(title='T', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Noise', statement='n', why='w', slug='noise'), dict(name='Captions', statement='Captions are words for each picture.', why='w')])}), 'Make comics')
test_eq([s['status'] for s in wj.steps], ['known', 'todo'])
```

[`set_here`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#set_here)
keeps the last idea that you opened in a walk of the course. It writes
only when the idea changed, or after a minute, so a page that loads
again does not write each time.
[`active_course`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#active_course)
is the course that you used last, for Today.

### A course from a rabbit hole

“I don’t get X” has three depths: a quick primer, a side walk, or its
own course. For a big gap, such as “diffusion model” on a step of a
paper,
[`course_from`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#course_from)
makes a course to learn X, with the place that it came from as `origin`:
the walk and the step (`{walk, step}`), or a local page (`{page}`). The
course gets your data from the walk. It has no stage yet: the course
page asks where you start, then plans the stages, as for any goal. The
same idea from the same place gives the same course, so a second tap
opens it again.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2759"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*Keep the time that you went back from course `cid` to the place that it

### course_from

``` python
def course_from(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, slug:str, origin:dict
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The course to learn concept `slug` as its own goal, linked to the place
`origin` (`{walk, step}` or `{page}`) that it came from.*

A walk with your data opens a course on a big idea at its step. The
course keeps the origin and the data, and has no stage yet. A second
call gives the same course.

``` python
l = temp_learning()
for n in ('Noise', 'Diffusion model'): l.put(n, f'{n} is one idea.', 'ml')
l.put_journey(dict(id='paper', title='A paper', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='noise')], data=[dict(path='~/pics', note='')]))
rc = course_from(l, 'diffusion-model', dict(walk='paper', step=0))
test_eq((rc.title, rc.origin['walk'], rc.origin['idea'], rc.data, rc.stages), ('Diffusion model', 'paper', 'noise', [dict(path='~/pics', note='')], []))
test_eq(course_from(l, 'diffusion-model', dict(walk='paper', step=0)).id, rc.id)
test_eq(courses_from(l, 'paper', 'noise').attrgot('id'), [rc.id])
```

A page origin is a local path only. A walk with no such step, or an idea
that is not there, is refused.
[`go_back`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#go_back)
keeps the time that you went back.

``` python
test_eq(course_from(l, 'noise', dict(page='/c/diffusion-model')).origin['page'], '/c/diffusion-model')
for bad in (dict(page='//evil.example/'), dict(page='https://evil.example/'), {}): test_fail(lambda: course_from(l, 'noise', bad), contains='local page')
test_fail(lambda: course_from(l, 'noise', dict(walk='paper', step=3)), contains='no step')
test_fail(lambda: course_from(l, 'nope', dict(walk='paper', step=0)), contains='no concept')
assert go_back(l, rc.id)['back_at'] and l.course(rc.id).origin['walk'] == 'paper'
```

## Find a source for each step

A source from the web for a walk step that has no passage, quoted word
for word and kept in your vault.

A walk from a paper or a link shows a passage of the source on each
step. A walk from a topic, and the walk of a talk from a path, often has
no source passage. Then the step shows the statement of the idea in the
tutor’s words. The learner cannot see where the knowledge comes from.

This module finds a source for such a step. It searches the web for the
idea, reads the best pages with plain HTTP (a paper with the paper
reader), and asks the model to quote one passage that explains the idea.
The tutor keeps the passage only when it is in the page word for word
and names the idea. Then it files the page in your vault, links it to
the concept, and keeps the passage on the step.

The rules are the rules of a link walk (`sources`): only public hosts,
plain HTTP with no browser, a cap on bytes, speed and time, and no fetch
on a request: the web app runs research only on its pool.

Import the modules that this module uses. `fossick` loads only when a
real search or fetch runs, so the import stays light.

### The query

The first query is the name of the idea, with its first alias when the
name does not hold it. A name of one word, or of words with many senses
(such as *Attention*), also gets the label of its subject
(`SUBJECT_LABEL`), so the search does not find pages from another field.
A page that explains the idea comes first, not a page on the topic of
the walk. When that search finds no good quote, a second query adds the
subject and the title of the walk, in at most 120 characters. The goal
text never goes to the search: a long goal with many words finds pages
on the goal, not on the idea. When a title is only the start of the
goal, it stays out, too. The search engine sees this text, so the Add
page says that the search sees your topic.

### Keep the source

[`file_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#file_page)
adds the page to the vault as a web document, as a link walk files a
page: its text, its title, its URL and the kind `web`. It never files
over a document: when the vault has the URL already and the stored text
has the passage, it uses that document. Else it files the new text as a
new document, with its own id, so older steps and links stay good.
[`ground()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#ground)
then finds it with your other sources.
[`link_concept`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#link_concept)
adds the page to the provenance of the concept, as
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract)
does, one entry for each document, so the concept page, the lessons and
the slides know where the idea comes from.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2845"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*Add the source `src` to the provenance of concept `slug`, under the

of the older one.*

### Research one step

[`research_step`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#research_step)
finds a source for step `i` of walk `j`. The search, the fetch and the
paper reader come in as functions, so a test uses fakes and no network.
It searches first for the idea by its name. When that finds no good
quote, it searches one more time with the subject and the title of the
walk
([`research_query`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#research_query)),
and skips the pages that it read. For each search it reads at most 3
candidates, one at a time: a web page with the fetch, a paper with the
paper reader
([`read_paper`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#read_paper)).
It stops at the first page with a good quote. A good quote is in the
page word for word and names the idea
([`names_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#names_idea)
from
[`ground`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#ground)):
the name word for word, or a key term (an alias, or a term such as
`LoRA`) and at least half of the other main words of the name. The
source line (the title of the page) counts with the quote. A weak match
is no source, as for a passage from your sources.

The paper reader files a paper before the model reads it. When the paper
has no good quote, research forgets it again, as a web page with no
quote is never filed. A paper that was in the vault before stays.

On the step it keeps the passage in `read` (as a passage from your
sources: its text, the title, the site, the URL and the vault document),
with `researched` and the time, and `research='found'`. It finds the
step again by its concept, under the lock of the walk, just before it
writes, so a step that moved or left the walk does not get the wrong
source. It clears the tutor note, and writes it again from the passage.
With no good page, the step gets `research='none'` and `research_why`,
one line that says why: the search found nothing, no page had a good
quote, or a page could not be read (with a short reason, such as a
certificate error). When the setting `research.on` is off, it does
nothing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L2918"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*Find a web source for step `i` of walk `j` (a walk or its id). Return

searches of
[`research_query`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#research_query).
With no source, the step gets `research_why`.

### Research a walk

[`to_research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#to_research)
gives the steps of a walk that want a source, in walk order, at most
`research.per_walk` of them.
[`mark_pending`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#mark_pending)
marks them `research='pending'` at once, so each step page can say
“Looking for a source…” while the pool works.
[`research_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#research_walk)
then researches them one by one, each found by its concept. A step that
has `none` or `found` already is not searched again. A step that is
pending is not searched again while its search runs. When a search stops
in a run, the step stays pending: after `research.retry` minutes,
[`to_research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#to_research)
takes it as not started. A restart stops each search. At start,
[`Researcher.resume`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#researcher.resume)
scans the walks on the research pool, and looks again at once for each
step that was pending before the start.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/path.py#L3006"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


demo, a note or a lesson. It keeps the jobs of each walk.*
